description: BP-1-like look of the Isaac Sim terrain for camera tests (isaac_landmarks.py). Status per value: Verified (in a source), Inferred (derived; derivation given), Assumed (placeholder).

shading.value: UsdPreviewSurface, roughness 1.0, metallic 0, specular workflow with specularColor 0 (no highlight)
shading.source: BP-1 is a fine basalt powder; treated as a matte Lambertian surface

albedo_luminance.source: middle of 0.10-0.12; no visible-light BP-1 albedo found in a source

tint_rgb_linear.source: measured by the coordinator on the BP-1 mound flanks in guidebook 2027 Figure 7 under that photo's lighting (refs/guidebook2027)

diffuse_rgb_linear.source: tint scaled so Rec.709 luminance 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B = 0.11

albedo_variation.value: x (1 + 0.15 u), u uniform in [-1, 1], independent per 1 cm height-field vertex (vertex colour primvar, interpolated across triangles)
albedo_variation.source: fine variation; the 2 cm gravel is already in the height field

rut_albedo.source: no data on how compacted wheel tracks change BP-1's appearance

walls_and_obstacles.value: same material as the terrain (one mesh)

lighting_diffuse.value: dome light only (uniform overhead sky), intensity 1500, fixed exposure (auto exposure off)

lighting_low.value: distant light 15 deg above the horizon (intensity 250000) plus a dome at 300, fixed exposure
lighting_low.source: arena lighting is unknown; low light shows ruts by their shadows
